I finished the queue-pids work on branch `worktree/resources-queue-pids`; it is not merged, pushed or restarted.

- **Commits:**
  - `026c992c1` has the code and both tests.
  - `08ce24ed7` has the docs: `Servex/doc/processes.md` (new "Who started this pid" section) and the `public/framework/ai/sessions/readme.md` "How to find things" paragraph.
  - `ea15a1fd9` is on main and edits `finding.md`.
- **Tests:**
  - `SpawnLog.test.mjs` passes 5 of 5.
  - `Gate-loud.test.mjs` is the queue test and passes. It checks one `queued` line (with `commit_pct` and `page_file_mb`), one `started` line, and no second `queued` line for a restored entry.
  - `Crumbs.test.mjs` passes and `node --check` is clean on every touched file.
  - `Gate-stale.test.mjs` can't run in this worktree because `Servex/node_modules` isn't copied here; that is unrelated to my change. `Gate-loud.test.mjs` borrows the main tree's packages through a loader hook, with no link.
- **No-agent rate:** about 12 async spawns a minute (7,724 over 10.6 h). The four pollers I skip make up about 9 of those, so the `spawns` log gets about 3 start lines a minute, each with an exit line.
- **Skipped callers:**
  - By name: `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, `netstat`, `git worktree list`, and `git rev-parse --verify --quiet`.
  - Not logged at all: sync spawns, which have no live pid to report, and the Bash tool's children of a claude.exe. The processes doc notes both limits, plus a `⬜` line for a PostToolUse hook.
- **Your three changes:**
  - The exit line is now `{"pid_exit":n,"code":…,"signal":…,"at":…}`.
  - The `queued` line carries `page_file_mb`. It is always null for now because the process monitor has no page-file reading yet.
  - `finding.md` rows 42-43 now have real `git grep` searches.
- **Readmes touched:** `Servex/doc/processes.md`, `public/framework/ai/sessions/readme.md`, and `public/framework/ai/sessions/doc/finding.md`.
- **Task log:** the completion is recorded in my own task log.

Branch `worktree/resources-relief` is ready to merge, and my task is complete. I haven't merged, pushed or restarted Servex.

**What the 726 kept were:** 717 were dormant agent rows, which run nothing, plus 6 standing agents and 3 servers. The sweep couldn't match agents to landed tasks because it never looked in `ai/sessions/` where today's tasks live, and dormant rows read zero turns. It now walks `sessions/` too and handles dormant rows. A dry run went from 0 to close / 726 kept to 47 to close / 7 kept.

**Commits:** `c9bdf7e5a` (pool never removes a held slot, sweep fix), `6fa25dcc8` (idle agent burning a core for 5 minutes goes dormant), `0c5ae8989` (`Servex/Relief.js` with its test and wiring in `Servex.js`).

**Relief:** at 70% commit it runs at most once per 15 minutes. It runs the sweep, stops finished worktrees' servers, sleeps idle agents, and counts reaped orphans. If commit is still at the line, it posts one risk note per episode naming the five biggest apps that aren't ours, and re-arms below 65%. It never kills anything outside our own closers.

**Docs:** `Servex/doc/processes.md` has the new "Early relief at 70%" and "A spinning idle agent" sections plus the sweep finding. `Servex/doc/pool.md` has the adopt race.

**Tests:**
- `node Servex/Relief.test.mjs`: 7 checks pass.
- `node Servex/pool-adopt-race.test.mjs`: 6 checks pass.
- `node Servex/processes.test.mjs`: 47 checks pass.
- `node Servex/closeout.test.mjs`: 12 checks pass.
- `pool-hold`, `pool-heal` and `pool-restore`: all pass.
- `node --check` is clean on every touched file.

**Caveat:** Relief has only run against fakes, never against the live machine. The first real run will be after the merge and a Servex restart.

I sent mastermind-resources the fixes for the leaks proposal and logged the flag, and I did not rewrite the file myself because the agent is still working. `text-check` found nothing in the folder, so the problems below came from reading `requirements.md`.

- **Title:** it is 22 words long. I proposed "Servex processes: every start gets an end".
- **Paragraphs:** the worktree and safety rules, the "what exists" paragraph and the first bullet of section 2 are each over 60 words. I gave the agent a bulleted split for the first one.
- **Checklist:** the Done line is prose. I asked for one tickable `- [ ]` line per deliverable (field rename, sampled children, `leaks.mjs` and `report.md`, the Chrome-pin test, docs) so the landing outcome can tick each with proof.

I didn't shoot any pages, since this is a proposal with no page.
That inbox line is my own earlier report echoed back, so there's nothing new to act on. The rewrite is with mastermind-resources and the flag is logged. I'm stopping here.

The leaks task is done and committed on `worktree/resources-leaks` (commits `31e4c0aaa` and `903ef92b5`). It is not merged, and I've sent the six-line report to `mastermind-resources`.

- **Live leaks:** none. No process is alive with its owner done, and 13 are alive with their owner still working. The one "gone" row is a junk line a test wrote into the main tree; the test is fixed, and I left the line because that log is append-only.
- **Causes fixed:** three paths left a start line open. The Browser exit hook and the browser watchdog both closed a chrome without writing its end line. A forced kill of a whole tree skipped the end lines of the servers inside it, and a new `Lifecycle.end_killed` now writes them (called from `Lifecycle.close()` and `Pool.kill`).
- **Safety guards:** the owner's Chrome, Code and Figma can no longer be ended by `--stop`, `kill()` or the watchdog. This includes a pid that Windows has reused for the owner's Chrome.
- **Report:** `leaks/report.md` in the task folder, in the main tree and uncommitted.
- **Tests:** these all pass: `chrome-pin`, `leaks`, `Lineage`, `processes`, `SpawnLog`, `Gate-loud`, `Crumbs` and `closeout` (12 checks). `closeout` failed twice under load, then passed on a clean rerun. The `closeout` failures were in step 6, which tests `Worktrees.js` (not edited); I did not find the cause.
- **Outside the fence:** I edited `Server/browser-watchdog.mjs`, which the brief's fence list doesn't name, because it is the Browser close path.

The review fixes are in one commit, 67ffc724c on `worktree/resources-leaks`. It is not merged. I've sent the two-line reply to `mastermind-resources`.

Fixes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 11 are done; 8 and 10 are skipped as you said. The `chrome-pin`, `leaks`, `Lineage` and `processes` tests pass, and `node --check` is clean on the touched `.js`/`.mjs` files.

- **Fix 4:** I added the pid 101 `pid_exit` line to the `process-monitor/task.jsonl` in the main tree with `LogLine.raw`, because `append.mjs` refuses pid lines.
- **Fix 6:** I took the simplest fail-closed option. `Lifecycle.kill()` kills a pid only when its command line is known and is not an owner's app. If the process list lacks the pid, it reads that one pid's command line first. If that read fails or the process isn't running, it leaves the pid alone. The new `killable()` and `process_now()` in `Servex/Lifecycle.js` do this. No test covers the case where the process list is unset.
- **Fix 7:** In `chrome-pin.test.mjs` the headed Chrome now uses a `playwright_chromiumdev_profile` marker in its `--user-data-dir`.
- **Fix 9:** The extra tab was on the `watch_spin` line at `Servex/Processes.js:147`, not 449 as the review said.
- **Fix 11:** The line is in `Servex/readme.md` "Where the code is".

The cause is committed as f9faeadc8 on `worktree/resources-leaks`, and I've sent the two-line reply to `mastermind-resources`. None of the branch's tests kill the dev server.

**Cause:** Servex's own sweep killed the worktree dev server at 23:00:07. Its end line in `lifecycle.jsonl` reads "reaped: its task … has landed". I had landed the task before the merge, and `Lifecycle.kept()` only spared servers whose task asked for a preview.

**Fix:** `kept()` now also holds the dev server of any unmerged worktree branch for up to 48 hours. It uses a new `WorktreePreview.unmerged()` in `Server/WorktreePreview.mjs`.

**Checks:**
- Run one at a time, `leaks`, `Lineage`, `processes`, `chrome-pin`, `SpawnLog` and `closeout` (12 checks) all left port 52533 up.
- I added assertions at the end of `Server/WorktreePreview.test.mjs`. That test can't import in this worktree because `Servex/node_modules` is missing here, so I ran the same checks in a scratch script instead and they passed.

I restarted the worktree server with `worktree-restart`. The cause is logged in `leaks/session.jsonl`, though it cites `Lifecycle.js` by approximate line (~301 and ~351) rather than exact `file:line`.

The review is in `errors/review.md`. This change has no page, so it covers only Requirements and Words, with no screenshots.

**The fix:**
1. Task `o25d5dte` in `mastermind-resources/session.jsonl:13` still says "queued". Nothing marks it started, links it to the `errors/` folder, or names the branch or commit `b332e4ea7`. The only trace is a free-text log line.

**Notes (worth a look, nothing must change):**
- **No test of the wiring:** the test calls `ErrorLine.note()` directly. Nothing proves that a tool which throws inside `server()` or `MCP.call()` writes exactly one line and still returns its error to the agent.
- **Volume:** every error a tool throws now writes a line, including agents' own mistakes like bad arguments. Busy session logs may fill with lines that aren't bugs.
- **Timestamp key:** the new line stamps `ts`, as the logging contract asks; the older process-id lines use `at` instead.

**What already holds up:**
- **The line:** `error` is the first key, followed by `where`, `tool` and `agent`.
- **The agent still gets its error:** both catch points return the error result to the agent as before.
- **No second error:** writing the line can never throw.
- **The option is wired:** the setting passed in `Servex.js` reaches `MCP.call()`.
- **The test passes:** `ErrorLine.test.mjs` passes in the worktree.
- **Docs are up to date:** the Servex readme, `doc/tool-process.md` and section 5 of indexing-past-work describe the new line, and I found nothing new left unlisted.

The verdict is **fix**. The code does what the owner asked, but the ask itself is recorded nowhere in the task folder, and the Servex readme doesn't list `Relief.js`. The review is in `mastermind-resources/review.md`.

**What was asked:** there is no `requirements.md` in the folder. The ask exists only in the agent's raw transcript, as a voice-app message at 06:16Z on 2026-11-07. It had four parts:
- write the 48 GB page file up as a recommendation: it helps short peaks, not leaks;
- say that tracking every process start and exit is the real fix;
- never close the owner's own apps, only suggest it, and only when they seem away from the PC;
- send voice-app the doc path so it can close its page-file task.

**Two things must change:**
1. **The ask isn't recorded.** There is no brief and no task line for this change, so a fresh agent couldn't pick it up from the folder. A brief or task should quote that message and link commit `9433a47e2` on branch `worktree/relief-idle-note`.
2. **`Servex/readme.md` doesn't list `Relief.js`.** Its link to `doc/processes.md` also leaves out the early-relief and page-file sections.

**Worth a look, nothing must change:**
- Nothing in the folder shows voice-app was sent the doc path yet.
- Two comments in `Servex/Processes.js` (lines 77 and 121) say the idle reading is only for `Games.js`; `Relief.js` reads it now too.
- A held note is only re-checked at the next relief run, every 15 minutes. An absence of 10 to 14 minutes can fall between runs and be missed. Checking on the 1-minute tick would be simpler.

**What holds up:** the note waits until there has been no keyboard or mouse input for 10 minutes. The process monitor really does provide that reading. The owner's apps are only ever named in a suggestion, never closed. The page-file section of `processes.md` covers peaks versus leaks clearly. `node Servex/Relief.test.mjs` passed all 9 checks in the worktree.

This change touched no page, so the review covers only Requirements and Words, with no screenshots.

The `pid-accounting` proposal is clear, so I made no rewrite. `node Server/text-check.mjs` on its folder printed no flags (`[]`). The title states the question. The five deliverables are numbered, and the report shape and the "Never" list are explicit.

I logged one "clear" line in `.claude/skills/clarity/flags.jsonl`.

All five deliverables are done. Summary of what landed:

**Measured** (`Servex/pid-coverage.mjs`, committed, read-only): 1,478 process starts in 24h — claude.exe/chrome end and attribute near 100%, node/git/other end near 99% but attribute 12–70% (expected: unowned `spawns`-log polls and sampling misses). ~150 shells sampled vs ~3,280 Bash/PowerShell tool calls in the same window — about 1 in 22 ever seen (can't leak, since they're gone before the next 10s sample).

**Found the real bug**: two sessions (`73e88e75`, `d2507b09`, plus `00c47a44`) got zero pid lines for their entire life because a mastermind reused `Servex/agents/roles/mastermind.md`'s "fallback when Servex is down" `claude -p` recipe for an ordinary `spawn_agent` pool refusal — a case where Servex is up and should have been retried or queued instead. (`1acd3902` turned out to be a normal, fully-tracked minion, not a bypass.) None of the three are still running.

**Fixed** (commit `08d1c600f`, `worktree/pid-accounting`, not merged): restricted that fallback's wording to "Servex itself unreachable," forbade it for a refusal, and documented both gaps in `Servex/doc/processes.md`.

**No unowned running processes** right now (`leaks.mjs`: 0 leaks; all 11 live claude.exe accounted for — 9 are the owner's desktop app, 2 are tracked Servex sessions). Never killed anything.

Full writeup: `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-resources/pid-accounting/report.md`.
**fixed**, head `d19b24dd2` (worktree `pid-accounting`); report.md committed `82497fe3e` in the main tree.

The `updates-rework` proposal is clear, and I made no rewrite.

- **Text check:** `node Server/text-check.mjs` on the task folder returned no flags.
- **Ten seconds:** the title ("one place per conversation, logs as the source of truth") and the owner's quote state the ask.
- **Layout:** the five-step plan is a numbered list. I did not shoot it, since the file is a brief for agents and has no page.

One `clear` line is appended to `.claude/skills/clarity/flags.jsonl`.

All 5 steps are built, tested, and committed on the `updates-rework` branch in the worktree.

**Commits:**
- `fc2108206` — steps 1, 2, 3, 5: `External.updates()` now keys its cursor by conversation (or the resolved voice session, or the bare caller), stored in `logs/inbox/<caller>.cursors.json` beside the legacy `.cursor` file; a brand-new key starts at "now" with a `missed` digest; `Follow` no longer pushes a followed `.jsonl`'s lines to an external agent's inbox — `updates` reads them itself and tags each `{agent, session, path}`; `updates` returns a digest by default (`raw: true` for every line); `deliver()` rotates the inbox into a monthly archive, losing nothing unread.
- `6cd95a17f` — step 4: `Agents.wake_parent` skips a repeated "done" to an external parent after stripping timestamps/ids (`Servex/agents/mark-strip.js`, its own file so it's testable without the Claude SDK).
- `84191b96b` — the `RemoteMCP.INSTRUCTIONS` sentence telling the voice agent to pass its `conversation` id.

**Tests:** `node Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.test.mjs` and `node Servex/agents/mark-strip.test.mjs` — both green.

**Not done / known gap:** `Servex/agents/External.test.mjs` cannot run in this worktree — `Agents.js`'s first import is `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, which isn't installed anywhere on this machine. Confirmed via `git show` on an earlier commit that this import predates my changes, so it's a pre-existing environment gap, not something this task introduced.

**Docs updated** (same commits as the code): `Servex/ext/remote/doc/catch-up.md` (moved items from "Not built" to "What is built") and `Servex/doc/follow.md`'s cloud-agent section.

All seven fixes are built and committed: `42baeffa3`.

- **A** — `followed_lines()` now takes a budget and stops at a line boundary once spent; a 60-line burst with a 50-line cap comes back 50 then 10, nothing lost or repeated.
- **B** — filters (`skip_by`/`heard`/`worth_waking`) now apply to followed lines, and `agent` is `sub.of ?? line.by`, never the follower's own id.
- **C** — a directory follow reuses `Follow`'s own tracked files (`follow.offsets`) instead of walking the tree on every call.
- **D** — `rotate()` decides from a cheap first-line read before touching the whole inbox; a cursor stale 7+ days no longer pins rotation forever.
- **E** — the duplicate-done skip now drops only the message to the parent, not the inbox write or the Next: note. Measured against the real `voice-app.jsonl` (read-only, 727 lines): of 398 "done" lines, only 4 (1.0%) were literal repeats — smaller than the original noise estimate, worth knowing for expectations.
- **F** — `Servex/node_modules` installed in the worktree so `External.test.mjs` and `Follow-ack.test.mjs` run here.
- **G** — `catch-up.md` and `follow.md` updated in the same commit.

Tests: `RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, `External.test.mjs`, `Follow-ack.test.mjs`, `mark-strip.test.mjs` all green.

All 4 review findings fixed and committed: **`04a559893`**.

1. `Servex/agents/doc/external.md` brought current (cursors-per-conversation, digest/raw, follows-via-updates, rotation, `mark-strip.js`), linking `catch-up.md` for detail.
2. `Servex/agents/map.md` gained a row for `mark-strip.js`/its test and a refreshed `External.js` one-liner.
3. `followed_lines` with budget 0 now reports `more: true` via a stat-only check (no read, no offset touched) when a followed file has unread bytes. Along the way, found and fixed a real bug this exposed: the `updates` tool never forwarded `cap` from its arguments at all — it was silently always 50 no matter what was asked.
4. `_done_seen` is now bounded at 500 entries with oldest-first eviction.

Tests: `RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, `External.test.mjs`, `Follow-ack.test.mjs`, `mark-strip.test.mjs` — all green.

done: `44afb979f`. Both test gaps closed — truncation and half-written-line coverage for `followed_lines`. All four tests (`RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, `External.test.mjs`, `Follow-ack.test.mjs`, `mark-strip.test.mjs`) green.

Idle — task landed. Last work was commit `44afb979f` (closing the last two review-flagged test gaps for the `updates-rework` branch); all four reviews on it have come back clean, all four tests green. Waiting on whether the mastermind wants anything further before merge.
Idle — task landed at commit `44afb979f`, all reviews clean, all four tests green. Nothing to act on.

Both deliverables are implemented, tested, documented and committed in the worktree:

- **149fe5e63** — `Processes.reap()` now also ends a "burning" orphan: a search-kind process (grep/egrep/fgrep/find/rg/du/xargs/ls, or `git grep`/`git log -S`) averaging ≥25% of one core over 2 minutes, logged as `{type:"reaped", why:"burning", cpu_avg, ...}`. The idle rule is untouched.
- **a91f41936** — `server-guard.mjs` now refuses an unscoped `grep -r`/`find`/`rg` rooted at `/`, a drive root, `~`/`$HOME`, `..`, or the repo/worktree root (named explicitly or via `cwd`), telling the agent to name a folder or use `git grep` instead. Docs (`Processes.js` header, `doc/processes.md`, the hook's own header, `.claude/hooks/readme.md`) updated in the same commits.

`Servex/processes.test.mjs` (108 checks) and `.claude/hooks/server-guard.test.mjs` (60/60) both pass; `node --check` is clean on both edited files. Reported to the mastermind-resources task log and stopping here per the brief.

The proposal `dev-server-count/requirements.md` is clear. `node Server/text-check.mjs` flagged nothing, and the title and "Why" section state the point at once. The four deliverables are numbered and the verification steps are concrete. It is a brief for agents, so there was nothing owner-facing to rewrite. I logged a "clear" line in `flags.jsonl`.
